lines.t: Lanternmoor clings to a hillside of grey rock, every doorway hung with a lamp that has not been allowed to go out.
The mine mouth at the east end of the street is boarded shut. A black gallows is chalked across the planks, with a fresh crack in the chalk where something has pushed from inside.
Miners sit on the steps with their hands wrapped round tin cups, not drinking. Nobody has been below in eleven days.
The stairs end in a cavern draped with white. Silk hangs from every beam, thick as sailcloth, and it moves though there is no wind.
Somewhere ahead, many small legs are tapping on stone. The tapping stops as you step onto the floor.
The tunnel opens into a vault the size of a chapel. At its centre, a seam of pale stone glows in the rock like a vein of milk.
Something the colour of old bruises hangs above it, wrapped in layers of silk. It unfolds one leg, then another, then eight.
The glow in the seam answers the glow in your palm. The Matriarch lowers herself from the ceiling, and hisses.
The Spider Matriarch folds in on herself like a closing hand. The silk falls away, strand by strand.
The seam beneath her pulses once, bright as a lamp, and then dims to a faint thread. Fresh cart tracks lead out of the vault, north.
Hask took what was here. The spiders only guarded what was left.
In the dust, a single chip of the pale stone is still warm. You pocket it.
